scorecards.inningsCommentary: West Indies embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 296 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. KC Brathwaite anchored the innings with a resolute 59, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. CAK Rajitha (2/23) maintained tight lines for Sri Lanka, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Dismissed for 147/5 (60.3 ov), West Indies succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as Sri Lanka's bowlers closed out the victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Daren Sammy National Cricket Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Sri Lanka posted 253/10 (78.7 ov) in their opening innings. In response, West Indies countered with 300/10 (100.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 8-Wicket Spell: ST Gabriel (8/58), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, ST Gabriel delivered a masterclass for West Indies (3 Runs & 13 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Match Drawn 47%) and allowing Match Drawn to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Sri Lanka faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Match Drawn's bowling unit, bolstered by LD Chandimal (158 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Match drawn in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Match Drawn's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Sri Lanka produced fighting phases, Match Drawn won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
